requirements.description: MIR-002 reports an empty applicable set as NOT_APPLICABLE
requirements.notes: The audit-findings dimension reports NOT_APPLICABLE when no registered audit names the checkpoint as its corrective delivery, PASS when every applicable finding is closed, and FAIL when one is not.

requirements.description: MIR-003 is analysed on its own and repaired on its own terms
requirements.notes: The mandatory-attack dimension derives its battery from the sealed Red Team reports of the same audits; an empty battery is NOT_APPLICABLE, an unexecuted mandatory attack is FAIL.

requirements.description: The overall verdict treats NOT_APPLICABLE as non-failing without rewriting it
requirements.notes: A report fails only on a FAIL. An inapplicable dimension keeps its own status in the artifact, is counted separately, and is never mapped to PASS.

requirements.description: Every NOT_APPLICABLE carries a reason, an empty expected count and a source
requirements.notes: An inapplicable dimension records status, reason, expectedCount zero, derivationSource and evidence, so it is auditable rather than a silent skip.

requirements.description: NOT_APPLICABLE never becomes a bypass
requirements.notes: The applicable set is derived from the canonical sources at every call and no caller or delivery artifact supplies it; checkpoint validation re-derives the registry-bound dimensions instead of believing the report.

requirements.description: A checkpoint with no open audit passes the real mirror
requirements.notes: A checkpoint that corrects no audit obtains a passing mirror through the shipped CLI, with the two empty dimensions recorded as NOT_APPLICABLE.

requirements.description: The first checkpoint of the next Gate reaches READY_FOR_REVIEW
requirements.notes: The whole transition is executed in a disposable repository: SETUP sealed, independent audit, derived milestone PASS, first checkpoint of the next Gate, READY_FOR_REVIEW. No Gate 0 work exists in this repository.

requirements.description: A real open finding still fails
requirements.notes: A non-empty applicable set with an unsatisfied item fails and the delivery cannot be sealed, so the repair is not a vacuous pass.

requirements.description: An expected audit artifact that is absent fails, and is never inapplicable
requirements.notes: When the canonical sources name a finding and the closure record is missing, the dimension fails rather than reporting an empty set.

requirements.description: A forged empty expected set does not reduce the applicable set
requirements.notes: A delivery declaring that it has nothing to close is ignored: the canonical derivation prevails and the open item still fails.

requirements.description: A milestone with no findings of its own can pass

requirements.description: A delivery with closed findings passes
requirements.notes: Three applicable findings, all CLOSED, and two mandatory attacks, both defended, produce a passing mirror.

requirements.description: A delivery with an open finding does not pass
requirements.notes: Three applicable findings with one OPEN produce a failing mirror and an unsealable delivery.

requirements.description: Every sealed checkpoint still validates under the new semantics
